review.summary: Attempt 4 of the phase-governance chunk closes every attempt-03 finding and every governance-scoped finding from the rejected phase attempt-01, with real code, real tests and lockstep documentation, and the recorded check evidence is genuine, complete and source-bound. The attempt-03 medium (docs/CI.md:181-195 claimed a dependency audit the phase-21 gate did not run, leaving ci.yml:62-69 consumerless) is fixed by adding the audit rather than by weakening the claim: tools/check_phase.py:166 now selects `scripts/check-dependencies.py --output docs/checks/phase-21-dependencies.json`, tools/test_ci.py:60-67 asserts the documented `## Scripts run by the current contracts gate` inventory equals the executed subset with both scripts present and no phase-21 exemption, and tools/test_ci.py:159-171 now ties the locked-graph preparation ordering to a command that actually consumes it. The committed-range hygiene low is fixed structurally at check_phase.py:161-164 (`git diff --check 0a213fe..HEAD -- .` with all three vendor YAML exclusions), guarded by tools/test_management_phases.py:320-323 and by tools/test_ci.py:44-53, which requires `fetch-depth: 0` whenever phase 21 or a ranged check is routed (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:25). The permissive-default low is fixed (review_phase.py:69 `completed_prior=0`) along with fail-closed `is_file()` guards on every prior-attempt artifact read (review_phase.py:104, 107, 117), covered by test_missing_prior_artifacts_are_sanitized_gate_errors. The scope-mutability low is fixed properly: chunk declarations now carry ordered immutable `scope_revisions` validated at review_phase.py:228-245, `verify_attempt_sequence` re-checks each prior record against the revision in force at that attempt and against its preserved prompt text (125-130), and test_scope_revision_history_preserves_old_reviews_and_rejects_rewrites proves that rewriting or narrowing a revision invalidates rather than silently rebinds an accepted record — this chunk's own history (from_attempt 1/3/4, 4→8→9 paths) is recorded accordingly at docs/phase-status.json:5097-5134, and the attempt-02 rejection at 41/50 is now explicit in the per-review `decisions` map (5171-5179), closing the phase-01 disposition findings. docs/RELEASE.md:160-166 now names the 0.1.1/0.2.0/0.2.1/0.2.2 deliveries and the authorizing management 0.86.0 plan. Check evidence verifies independently: docs/reviews/phase-21-chunk-phase-governance-attempt-04.checks.json is byte-identical in content to docs/checks/phase-21.json, carries source_sha256 ae5352b1…, source_unchanged true, passed true, no `scope` key (so review_phase.check_evidence:211 would not accept a contracts-only receipt), and its 25 command entries match my hand reconstruction of commands_for(21) element for element and in order (check_phase.py:154-175), every exit_code 0 and timeout false, with test_red_team_management 28/28, test_management_phases 21/21, test_review_phase 51/51 and test_ci 35/35 green in captured stderr, and a private-material scan executed 32 seconds earlier at the same fingerprint (docs/checks/phase-21-private-material.json:3-8: 1894 files, zero credential and zero new tenant occurrences). Later phases stay fail-closed: red_team_management.py:514-515 raises unconditionally for `--require-through-phase` above 21, management_commands drops the version-specific release helper and rewrites inherited phase-19/20 receipt paths, and phase 21 deliberately omits native_exports/live_evidence per the documented evidence-scope boundary at docs/PHASES.md:195-203. The no-cargo boundary is sound for this source state: the only SDK-file exception is byte-proved except one 64-hex provenance hash (verify_planning_fixture, check_phase.py:93-120), and crates/scm-sdk/src/models/tests.rs:149-157 consumes only the frozen `baselineCommit` and `specimens`. What remains is small: `deny.toml` is the one policy input the newly added audit depends on that the frozen-input diff does not pin; two test assertions read stronger than they are (list-membership substring checks, unasserted bootstrap ordering); the manifest-consumer coverage list is hand-maintained; docs/PHASES.md:135 has not been extended with the dependency-audit and committed-range evidence the gate now requires; and the governance documents carry pervasive digits-glued-to-words typography. No blocker or high finding. Categories 9/9/8.5/9/9 = 44.5/50.

findings.description: The phase-21 frozen-input list (148-153) pins crates/scm-sdk, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, LICENSE, NOTICE and six ledgers against 0a213fe79c7f0c5758f05f53d04a5c577a4f3f4e, but not deny.toml. deny.toml is the enforced license/source/ban policy consumed by the dependency audit this attempt newly added to the gate (check_phase.py:166), and unlike rustfmt.toml — whose effect is self-detecting because tools/generate_models.py --check re-runs rustfmt and compares bytes — a relaxed deny.toml makes check-dependencies.py report passed (recorded output: packages 206, advisoryRevision 999ec89d…, passed true) without the gate noticing the policy itself moved. Phase 21 changes no dependencies, so nothing is wrong in this source state; the gap is that 'unchanged SDK inputs against the frozen baseline' (docs/PHASES.md:135) does not currently cover the configuration that decides the audit verdict.
findings.required_fix: Add "deny.toml" to the paths list at tools/check_phase.py:148-153 so the baseline diff and the untracked-file assertion both cover it, and extend tools/test_management_phases.py:320-323 to assert the dependency-policy configuration is part of the frozen set; or state explicitly in docs/PHASES.md:135 that dependency policy configuration is deliberately mutable during planning and name the phase that re-pins it.

findings.description: In test_future_milestones_require_explicit_complete_artifacts, `self.assertFalse(any("0.2.2" in c for c in commands))` tests list membership, not substring containment: `c` is a command list, so it only fails if some argument is exactly "0.2.2". A rewritten-but-still-version-bound argument such as docs/checks/phase-23-release-registry-0.2.2.json would pass. The same shape appears at line 154 (`"scripts/check-rust.py" in c`), where it happens to be correct only because that value is a standalone element. Nothing leaks today — the sole "0.2.2" literal arrives with scripts/check-access-release.py, which management_commands skips at check_phase.py:186 — so this is assertion precision rather than a live hole, but the test reads as a guarantee it does not provide for the inherited phase-22-25 command lists.
findings.required_fix: Replace the membership checks with argument-level substring checks, e.g. `self.assertFalse(any("0.2.2" in value for c in commands for value in c))`, and apply the same form to the historical-receipt-path assertions at lines 157-160 so inherited release-version literals cannot reappear inside a longer argument.

findings.description: test_node_matches_owned_pin_and_phase_gate_verifies_only asserts only that "tools/bootstrap_reference.py" appears somewhere in the workflow text. Since this chunk routes CI at commands_for(21), two of the 25 executed commands are `.local/typescript/node_modules/.bin/tsx tools/schema-oracle.mts --check` and `tools/node_modules/.bin/tsx tools/verify-gateway-specimens.mts --check`, neither of which exists until bootstrap_reference.py restores the frozen tree and symlinks .local/typescript/node_modules to tools/node_modules (tools/bootstrap_reference.py:43-50). The ordering is correct in .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:70-73 today, but it is unguarded, while the analogous cargo prerequisite ordering is asserted by index at test_ci.py:166-169. Reordering the restore step after the gate step would break the contracts job with every test still green.
findings.required_fix: In test_ci.py, resolve the contracts job step list and assert `lines.index("run: python3 tools/bootstrap_reference.py") < lines.index(phase)` whenever any selected command's argv[0] resolves under .local/typescript/node_modules or tools/node_modules, mirroring test_qualification_prepares_complete_locked_graph_before_offline_checks.

findings.description: test_plan_gate_covers_manifest_consumers_and_ci enumerates the manifest-dependent checks by hand (model_fixtures.py, generate_constants.py, response_defaults.py, schema-oracle.mts, verify-gateway-specimens.mts). Grepping contracts/manifest.json across tools/ returns seven non-test readers, of which tools/g25_audit.py is absent from commands_for(21) even though it ran under the previous phase-20 routing. The omission is harmless here because g25_audit.py reads only `['baseline']['commit']` (g25_audit.py:95), which the manifest change does not touch — but that justification exists nowhere in the repository, and the hardcoded list means a future manifest-consuming tool can be left out of the planning gate silently while the test still passes.
findings.required_fix: Derive the expected set instead of listing it: compute the tools that reference contracts/manifest.json and assert each is either selected by commands_for(21) or present in an explicit, commented exemption list stating why its manifest use is insensitive to the vendored-source change (for g25_audit.py: it reads only the frozen baseline commit).

findings.description: The phase-21 'Required evidence' cell lists baseline contracts/self-tests, provenance tampering tests, generation reproducibility, the private-material scan, unchanged SDK inputs against 0a213fe and accepted chunk/phase reviews, but not the two obligations this attempt added to the gate: the current dependency audit (check_phase.py:166, which also makes the planning gate network-dependent for RustSec advisory refresh) and the committed-range whitespace check from the frozen baseline through HEAD (check_phase.py:161-164). docs/CI.md:146-148 documents the ranged check and docs/CI.md:184-189 the audit, so the authoritative phase table is now the least current of the three scoped documents, and the chunk's own lockstep principle ('Update routing, tests and documentation together', docs/PHASES.md:150-151) is applied to CI.md and RELEASE.md but not to this row.
findings.required_fix: Extend the phase-21 required-evidence cell at docs/PHASES.md:135 to name the current dependency/advisory audit and the baseline-to-HEAD committed hygiene check, and note that the planning gate therefore requires network access for advisory refresh and full Git history for the ranged diff.

findings.description: The governance documents this chunk owns carry pervasive missing spaces before digits, which degrades the readability of the texts a maintainer consults under time pressure and makes the regex-based documentation guards fragile. Examples: docs/RELEASE.md:160 'covers the completed0.1.1 and0.2.0 deliveries' and :163 'management0.86.0 plan'; docs/CI.md:146-147 'the frozen0.2.2 baseline' and :167 'its59-command full gate and41-command contracts subset'; docs/PHASES.md:106 'least46/50', :118 'phase18 accepts', :128 'phases21–25', :135 'management0.86.0 bytes'. The counts regexes at tools/test_ci.py:118-128 and :135-146 currently match only because the numbers they capture happen to retain their spacing; the same glueing inside one of those sentences would turn a lockstep guard into an unexplained test failure.
findings.required_fix: Normalise the spacing before numerals across docs/PHASES.md, docs/CI.md, docs/RELEASE.md and the phase-21 notes in docs/phase-status.json, and keep the guarded count sentences (test_ci.py:118-128, 135-146) in their asserted form so the documentation tests fail loudly rather than silently stop matching.

evidence: Recorded evidence is complete, executed and source-bound. docs/reviews/phase-21-chunk-phase-governance-attempt-04.checks.json is identical in content to docs/checks/phase-21.json: phase 21, source_sha256 ae5352b1d69acc340c4c9b71352f3c25955d19b7a1dafd4be4a39f046b69860c (equal to the reviewed hash in my prompt), source_unchanged true, checked_at 2026-10-19T13:27:09, passed true, and no "scope" key, so review_phase.check_evidence:210-217 would accept it and would reject a contracts-only receipt. I reconstructed commands_for(21) by hand from tools/check_phase.py:135-175 (4 phase-21-specific commands, the 10-command `common` block in order, then check-dependencies, test_ci, the three --check tools, verify_native_fixtures, red_team_dataplane, schema-oracle, verify-gateway-specimens, generate_validation, generate_models) and it matches the 25 recorded entries element for element and in order; every exit_code is 0 with timeout false.

The attempt-03 medium is fixed by adding the audit, not by softening the claim. tools/check_phase.py:166 selects ["python", "scripts/check-dependencies.py", "--output", "docs/checks/phase-21-dependencies.json"] (recorded output: passed true, 206 packages, advisoryRevision 999ec89d5d3f10f20be14750ec8c2d8b44e0ac9b, freshHead true); docs/CI.md:152-156 lists exactly check-dependencies.py and check-private-material.py; tools/test_ci.py:60-67 asserts the documented inventory equals the executed subset's scripts/check-*.py set and that both are present, with no `if phase != 21` exemption; tools/test_ci.py:159-171 asserts cargo fetch precedes all-feature metadata precedes the gate and that some selected command consumes check-dependencies.py, so .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:62-69 again has a real consumer.

Committed-range hygiene is restored and machine-enforced. tools/check_phase.py:161-164 adds `git diff --check 0a213fe79c7f0c5758f05f53d04a5c577a4f3f4e..HEAD -- .` with the red-team-management, red-team-data-plane and portkey vendor YAML exclusions (recorded as check 4, exit 0); tools/test_management_phases.py:320-323 requires both the dependency audit and a ranged `git diff --check` containing MANAGEMENT_BASELINE..HEAD; tools/test_ci.py:49-53 requires fetch-depth 0 for phase 21 or any ranged check, satisfied by .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:25; tools/test_management_phases.py:120-124 still requires the management vendor exclusion on every ranged or unranged `--check` diff for phases 21-25.

Scope governance is now versioned and immutable per attempt. review_phase.declared_chunk_scope:228-245 requires a nonempty ordered `scope_revisions` list starting at from_attempt 1 with unique nonempty paths whose last revision equals the current scope, and resolves a historical attempt to the revision in force then; verify_attempt_sequence:125-130 re-checks each prior record's scope_evidence against that revision and against the exact `Chunk scope artifacts: [...]` line in its preserved prompt; verify_record:292-298 does the same for the record under test. docs/phase-status.json:5097-5134 records this chunk's three revisions (from_attempt 1/3/4; 4, 8 and 9 paths), and my prompt's nine artifacts match the from_attempt-4 revision exactly in order. test_scope_revision_history_preserves_old_reviews_and_rejects_rewrites proves that rewriting revision 1 invalidates the attempt-01 record and that dropping revisions raises.

The fifth-attempt exception and its default are strict. review_phase.gate_decision:69-86 defaults completed_prior to 0, rejects on any blocker/high finding before scoring, targets 42 for chunks and 46 for phases, and grants accepted_with_deficiencies only at attempt 5 with exactly four completed prior reviews, every category >=8 and a recorded finding or limitation; line 70 additionally rejects any phase-21 phase-level review scoring below 9/10, matching docs/PHASES.md:135. verify_record:272-275 recomputes the decision with the real count and rejects any mismatch, so a stale or fabricated decision cannot carry gate_passed true. test_failed_attempts_cannot_unlock_fifth_exception asserts rejection at total 41 for 0-3 completed priors and acceptance only at 4; test_plan_score_floor_cannot_be_bypassed_by_category_total asserts a 50/50 review scoring 8.5/10 fails phase 21.

Prior-artifact reads now fail closed. review_phase.py:104 and :117 guard each previous attempt's prompt, checks snapshot and CLI envelope with `not evidence.is_file() or evidence.is_symlink()`, and :107 raises "Previous review evidence has changed" before json.loads when a record is missing; test_missing_prior_artifacts_are_sanitized_gate_errors drives the .json, .prompt.md and .cli.json deletions and test_failed_invocation_consumes_attempt_without_dead_end drives all four failure reasons through main(), asserting the sanitized .failed.json receipt, completed==0 and prompt-tamper detection.

Later phases cannot pass on plan artifacts. tools/red_team_management.py:511-515 accepts --require-through-phase only in 21-25 and raises unconditionally above 21; management_commands adds that flag for 22-25, skips scripts/check-access-release.py when inheriting (check_phase.py:186), rewrites inherited phase-19/20 receipt paths to the active phase (188-189) — commands_for(20) having already normalised phase-17 paths to phase-20 at check_phase.py:213 — and appends both packaged compilers from phase 23 (197-200). test_future_milestones_require_explicit_complete_artifacts and test_qualification_has_both_packaged_compilers cover this; test_plan_retains_static_closure_without_claiming_current_live_proof asserts native_exports.py and live_evidence.py are absent from phase 21 and present in 23-24, matching the documented evidence-scope boundary at docs/PHASES.md:195-203.

The CI subset cannot qualify a review even though it currently equals the full list. check_phase.ci_commands_for:646-651 filters only native scripts (none of which phase 21 selects), check_phase.main:691-694 stamps scope "ci_contracts_only_not_full_phase_qualification" and writes phase-21-contracts.json, and check_evidence:211 requires `scope is None`; test_ci_subsets_cannot_replace_full_reports asserts a contracts receipt is rejected as "incomplete" for all five phases, and test_ci_contract_subset_cannot_replace_complete_phase_qualification asserts the workflow references phase-21-contracts.json and never phase-21.json. docs/CI.md:158-165 states the 25/25 equality, the separate scope marker and that neither local checks nor the job prove remote jobs passed.

The single SDK-file exception is byte-exact and its consumer is safe without cargo. check_phase.require_only_hash_replacements:79-90 requires each replaced value to be 64 lowercase hex characters occurring exactly once and compares full reconstructed bytes; verify_planning_fixture:93-120 applies it to crates/scm-sdk/src/fixtures/model-regressions.json and to the oracle corpus, resolves the corpus path from the baseline object so "source" cannot be redirected, rejects symlinks and requires the rebound manifest hash to equal current contracts/manifest.json bytes; verify_planning_gateway_proof:123-132 allows exactly the two allowlisted input hashes and fails closed if the allowlist is incomplete. crates/scm-sdk/src/models/tests.rs:147-164 consumes only baselineCommit and specimens from that fixture, both byte-frozen, so running no Rust check in this phase does not hide a regression in it.

Privacy evidence is fresh at the reviewed hash. docs/checks/phase-21-private-material.json:3-17 records checkedAt 13:26:37 (32 seconds before the gate run), sourceSha256 ae5352b1… identical to the reviewed fingerprint, sourceUnchanged true, passed true, 1894 git-visible files, 0 selected identity/secret matches, 132 published-crate candidates with 0 registration matches, and 3 tenant occurrences all pre-existing in HEAD with newOrChangedFilesCount 0. scripts/check-private-material.py:167-175 binds --check to the current source fingerprint and published-candidate fingerprint rather than to a commit, so the receipt stays valid in CI at the same tree; its reported receiptFresh/privateScanReexecuted false semantics are accurate and documented.

Review-request integrity matches the artifact I was given. review_phase.main:470-524 writes the checks snapshot only after refusing to overwrite an existing attempt (476), validates that every --scope-evidence path resolves inside the repository (472-475), rejects a supplied scope differing from the current declaration before launching Claude (480-482), and emits the exact prompt I received including the `Review scope: chunk.` prefix (546), the single Active follow-up plan line naming docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md, and the nine-artifact `Chunk scope artifacts:` line; the invocation is restricted to Read,Glob,Grep with an empty MCP config and a 25 USD budget (565-567), matching this session. test_cli_rejects_scope_mismatch_before_requesting_review asserts the reviewer is never called on a scope mismatch.

Disposition bookkeeping now matches the record. docs/phase-status.json:5148-5257 lists all six chunk attempt records, a per-review decisions map giving each attempt's decision, total and reviewed scope — including phase-governance attempt-02 as rejected at 41 (5171-5179) — and the rejected phase_review at 43/50 and 8.5/10 (5252-5257); private_scan_history:5260-5305 marks the authoritative receipt and classifies all seven superseded scans, including the interrupted one as passed false with no acceptance claim. docs/RELEASE.md:160-166 names the 0.1.1, 0.2.0, 0.2.1 and 0.2.2 deliveries and the management 0.86.0 plan authorization, closing the phase attempt-01 low that had been deferred three times.
limitations: Read-only review with no execution. I could not recompute any SHA-256, run git, or run the suites, so the reviewed source hash ae5352b1…, the stated checks snapshot hash 36ce2f96…, the private-material receipt binding and all 25 recorded exit codes are judged from the preserved prompt, the recorded snapshots and the source of the tools that produced them. My statement that the recorded command list equals commands_for(21) is a hand reconstruction of tools/check_phase.py:135-175, not an executed comparison.

No remote run of the re-pointed workflow exists. docs/checks/ contains no phase-21-contracts.json, so the phase-21 CI routing is configuration plus local guard evidence only. The job's 25 commands now additionally require network access for the RustSec advisory refresh and a restored .local/typescript tree for the two tsx oracles. docs/CI.md:158-165 and docs/PHASES.md:174-180 state this honestly and phase 21's acceptance criteria do not require remote CI, so I treat it as an unverified configuration rather than a finding.

The review evidence chain is self-referential by design. review_phase.py:15-16 excludes docs/reviews/, docs/checks/ and docs/phase-status.json from the source fingerprint, so record, prompt, CLI-envelope, snapshot and chunk-declaration integrity rests on hashes recorded inside those same unfingerprinted files; a consistently edited set is undetectable from inside this review. The scope_revisions mechanism added here closes the retroactive-rewrite path within that model, but the model itself is pre-existing and unchanged.

Scope was the nine declared phase-governance artifacts. I did not audit the plan-and-provenance chunk (contracts/airs-*.json, the vendored 0.86.0 tree, manifest ownership, tools/red_team_management.py internals) beyond the governance claims that depend on them — specifically its --require-through-phase fail-closed path and the manifest-consumer coverage question — and a sibling attempt-04 review of that chunk was in flight (its prompt and checks snapshot exist without a completed or failed receipt), so I make no claim about it.

I did not re-audit historical phase command lists beyond the inherited ones phases 22-25 reuse. I verified by reading commands_for(17)/(19)/(20) that no phase-12 or phase-17 receipt path can leak into a management phase, but I could not execute the inherited phase-22-25 lists, which fail closed by design.

Static governance evidence only. Nothing in this chunk certifies runtime behaviour, request construction, generated Rust correctness, union-order preservation, dependency advisory status at any later moment, live tenant acceptance, release readiness or phase 22-25 progress.

My low finding about deny.toml is a reasoning result, not an observation of a change: I could not run git, so I cannot state whether deny.toml or rustfmt.toml actually differ from 0a213fe in this branch. The finding concerns the gate's coverage, not an observed regression.
